name: Permutations avoiding long monotone progressions
description: construct() -> a permutation of 1..n=128. Minimize the longest subsequence whose values form an increasing OR decreasing nonconstant arithmetic progression; subsequence positions need not be adjacent. A known finite construction attains 2, so this is a rediscovery task. Permute [1,128] and minimize the longest arithmetic-progression subsequence, allowing either sign of the common difference. The known finite optimum is 2; infinite-permutation questions are not recreated here.

sources.locator: James A. Davis, Roger C. Entringer, Ronald L. Graham and Gustavus J. Simmons, On permutations containing no long arithmetic progressions. Acta Arithmetica XXXIV (1977), opening page visually inspected: finite permutations avoiding increasing and decreasing three-term progressions exist for every n, with the doubling construction proved explicitly.
